stem: A waitlisted candidate receives a transplant at the listing hospital. When must the program remove the candidate from the waitlist and notify OPTN?

options.text: Within 24 hours of the transplant or death event
Only on the five-year transplant anniversary
Within 90 days after the six-month follow-up form is due
Never; waitlist removal is optional after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Policy 3.9 requires registering transplant hospitals to remove candidates from waitlists and notify OPTN within 24 hours when a candidate receives a transplant or dies while awaiting transplant.

rationale_incorrect.B: Waitlist removal is required promptly after transplant or death, not deferred for years.
rationale_incorrect.C: Ninety-day follow-up form timing applies to post-transplant data submission, not waitlist removal.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist removal and OPTN notification within 24 hours are required, not optional.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.9 → Removing Candidates from the Waiting List
primary_anchor.quote_hint: remove the candidate from the hospital's organ waiting lists and notify the OPTN within 24 hours

references.locator: Policy 3.9 → Removing Candidates from the Waiting List (notify OPTN within 24 hours of transplant or death); PDF p. 53 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 020500 item; waitlist removal timing distinct from inactive accrual (cctc-2037/2045) and registration notice (cctc-2041); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 53.

stem: A patient with type 1 diabetes already has a functioning kidney transplant and now seeks pancreas transplantation. Which evaluation outcome description is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Pancreas after kidney (PAK) transplantation for diabetes with an existing kidney graft
Simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) transplantation before any kidney graft
Isolated liver transplantation for diabetes management
Pancreas transplant is never performed after a kidney graft

explanation.rationale_correct: Pancreas transplant alone or pancreas after kidney (PAK) transplantation is indicated for candidates with diabetes who already have a kidney transplant, distinct from simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: SPK is performed when diabetes and renal insufficiency are present together before kidney transplant, not after an existing functioning kidney graft.
rationale_incorrect.C: Diabetes management with an existing kidney graft is addressed through pancreas transplantation, not isolated liver transplant.
rationale_incorrect.D: PAK transplantation is a recognized option after kidney transplant for appropriate candidates.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Pancreas transplant alone (PTA) or pancreas after kidney (PAK) transplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → Indications → A. Pancreas transplant alone or pancreas after kidney (PAK); PDF p. 825 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 020300 item; third kidney_pancreas organ tag; PAK angle distinct from SPK suitability (cctc-2038); anchor verified on Cupples p. 825.

stem: When coordinating age- and gender-appropriate health-maintenance testing during transplant evaluation, which assessments are included in standard references?

options.text: Skin assessment and assessment of dentition
Only cosmetic dermatology procedures without clinical assessment
Dental evaluation is permanently contraindicated before transplant
Skin assessment is omitted for all transplant candidates

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation health-maintenance testing may include mammogram, Papanicolaou test, bone densitometry, colonoscopy, skin assessment, and assessment of dentition per national prevention guidelines.

rationale_incorrect.B: Health-maintenance screening includes clinical skin and dental assessment, not cosmetic procedures alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Dentition assessment is part of evaluation rather than being contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.D: Skin assessment is explicitly listed among health-maintenance evaluation components.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Colonoscopy Skin assessment Assessment of dentition

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → b.c.iii. (health-maintenance testing including skin assessment and dentition); PDF p. 97 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 020200 item; skin/dentition screening distinct from bronchoscopy (cctc-2043) and infectious disease consult (cctc-2034); anchor verified on Cupples p. 97.

stem: A postmenopausal transplant candidate with a smoking history is completing pretransplant evaluation. Which screening study should the coordinator arrange per standard references?

options.text: Bone densitometry to assess for osteopenia or osteoporosis
No bone health screening because immunosuppression prevents bone loss
Routine daily bone biopsy for every candidate
Bone screening deferred until ten years after transplant only

explanation.rationale_correct: Osteoporosis screening with bone densitometry is recommended for postmenopausal women and candidates with smoking history, chronic corticosteroid use, or cholestatic liver disease.

rationale_incorrect.B: Solid-organ transplant recipients are at increased bone-loss risk from immunosuppression and require assessment.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bone densitometry is the screening method referenced, not routine daily biopsy.
rationale_incorrect.D: Pretransplant osteoporosis screening is part of evaluation rather than deferred exclusively until ten years post-transplant.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: assessed for osteopenia or osteoporosis by bone densitometry

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → h. Osteoporosis screening (bone densitometry for postmenopausal women and smokers); PDF p. 31 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 020700 item; pretransplant bone densitometry distinct from liver HCC surveillance (cctc-2040) and kidney urine baseline (cctc-2016); anchor verified on Cupples p. 31.
